headline: 97% said skin felt less oily throughout the day
subhead: Apply 2-3 drops after cleansing & toning, in the PM.
footnote: Consumer study: 97% subjects said skin felt less oily throughout the day after using this serum for 2 weeks. This is subjects' own perception.
layout_description: Headline top-left, subhead below. Centre: one wide split frame divided by a thin vertical line with 'Day 0' and 'Week 2' labels, kept empty until real study photos are supplied. Real pack shot right 45%. Study footnote bottom.
image_prompt: Empty background scene only: a clean off-white surface divided by a very faint vertical seam into two slightly different pale tones, soft even light. Off-white, soft natural light, few props, clinical minimal style. Square 1080x1080. Keep the right 45% of the frame as an empty clear space, evenly lit and the left 50% calm and low-detail. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
photography_needed: Real, unretouched split photos from a documented 2-week study of this exact serum, with study ID, subject consent and lighting kept constant. Nothing is shown until they exist.
adaptation_notes: Sensorial angle from the F17 perception study (felt less oily). Perception stat stays a perception stat; time window and 'subjects said' qualifier are in the footnote. Kept: split frame with two time labels (Dr. Sheth's), from-X-to-Y structure (Re'equil, reworded), two-state arrangement (The Derma Co). Dropped: 7-day dark circle claim, 25% off block, ingredient icons, 'greasy to balanced' wording.

blend_sources.took: from-state to to-state arrangement above the pack

verdict.label: Fix before review
verdict.detail: Change the flagged lines, or attach the substantiation a reviewer would need to accept them.

findings.message: "Day 0 / Week 2" labels frame a before/after progression, which draws platform restrictions and needs representative, unretouched evidence.
findings.fix: Remove the Day 0 / Week 2 labels, or show only the study qualifier text.

findings.message: Statistics need their study qualifier on the creative and must not be worded more strongly than the study.
findings.fix: Quote the stat exactly as the study states it ('90% subjects said…') and add a footnote: study type (consumer perception / in-vivo / in-vitro), duration, and n if known.
findings.note: Wording appears on the product page (F17). Severity lowered one step: the brand has published it, but a reviewer must still confirm substantiation is on file.
